name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
description: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), a benchmark spanning 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages for evaluating text embedding models.
creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
rai:dataCollection: MTEB unifies 58 datasets from different embedding tasks into a common evaluation framework. It incorporates existing datasets such as SemEval STS datasets and BEIR, and also includes custom-made datasets for MTEB. The paper states that ArxivClusteringS2S/P2P, BiorxivClusteringS2S/P2P, and MedrxivClusteringS2S/P2P were custom-made for MTEB using the public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv. RedditClusteringP2P was created for MTEB using available data from Reddit posts, and StackExchangeClusteringP2P was created for MTEB using available data from StackExchange posts. Datasets and the leaderboard are available on the Hugging Face Hub.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Document analysis, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include existing public benchmark datasets and corpora reused in MTEB, including SemEval STS datasets, BEIR datasets, BUCC, Tatoeba, SummEval, Kaggle competition datasets, and others. For custom MTEB datasets, raw data came from public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv, available Reddit posts, and available StackExchange posts.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For clustering datasets custom-made for MTEB, S2S inputs use only paper titles, while P2P inputs concatenate title and abstract. For arXiv, when multiple categories can be given to a single paper, only the first one is used. For every dataset, split and strategy, subsets of labels are selected and articles are sampled from those labels, yielding splits with varying amount and size of clusters.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Several clustering tasks are framed as both S2S and P2P tasks; the former compare titles only, while the latter include title and content, e.g. for ArxivClustering abstracts are concatenated to the title in the P2P setting. MTEB imposes no limit on input length, leaving it up to models to truncate if necessary. Evaluation uses test splits of all datasets except MSMARCO, where the dev split is used following BEIR.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are inherited from the underlying datasets or created from existing human-provided metadata. The paper states that for custom arXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv clustering datasets, cluster labels are generated using categories given to the papers by humans. For bitext mining datasets, annotated pairs correspond to translated sentence pairs. For STS datasets, labels are continuous similarity scores. For summarization, human-written and machine-generated summaries are provided alongside human annotations. For reranking, AskUbuntuDupQuestions uses manual annotations marking pairs of questions as similar or dissimilar.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark aims for reproducibility through versioning at a dataset and software level. JSON files corresponding to all results in the paper have been made available with the benchmark. The authors welcome dataset, task, metric contributions via pull requests to continue development of MTEB, and additions to the leaderboard via an automatic submission format.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes datasets containing language information and multilingual coverage across 112 languages. Some included datasets explicitly involve user-generated or human text tied to domains such as Amazon customer reviews, online banking queries, Twitter messages, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, Alexa virtual assistant utterances, movie reviews, and toxic comments. The paper also mentions languages and, in examples, age and gender-like references may appear in text content, but no benchmark-level sensitive attribute collection protocol is described.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to make selecting the right embedding model easier and simplify future embedding research and industry applications of text embeddings by providing reliable performance estimates across diverse tasks.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that implementation details like preprocessing or hyperparameters may influence results. It also states that parts of SciDocsRR are likely included in the training data of some models, and that controlling for data contamination is challenging; overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets is ignored in MTEB scores. The paper also notes task imbalance: average scores are biased toward tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification and clustering.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper lists several limitations of MTEB: very long document datasets are missing; tasks are imbalanced, with summarization having only a single dataset, biasing average scores toward tasks with many datasets; multilinguality is incomplete because retrieval and clustering are English-only and multilingual retrieval cannot be comprehensively benchmarked; MTEB does not contain code datasets; and it focuses solely on natural language applications, not additional modalities. The paper also notes that no model claims state-of-the-art on all tasks and that controlling for training-data contamination is challenging.
rai:dataUseCases: MTEB is a benchmark for evaluating text embedding models across 8 tasks: bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity, and summarization. It is intended to provide reliable embedding performance estimates, establish baselines, support benchmarking of any embedding model through open-source code, and aid model selection for future research or industry applications. Evaluation is performed primarily on test splits, except MSMARCO where the dev split is used.
